solutions.question: Ten boys work on a petrol pump station. They get weekly wages as follows: Wages (in Rs.) 4250, 4350, 4400, 4250, 4350, 4410,4500, 4300, 4500, 4390. Find the arithmetic mean by short formula, median and mode of their wages.
steps: By short formula, X̄ = A + Σd ÷ n = 4350 + 200 ÷ 10 = Rs. 4370.
Arranging the wages in ascending order gives Rs. 4250, 4250, 4300, 4350, 4350, 4390, 4400, 4410, 4500, 4500.
Since n = 10 is even, X̃ = (5th observation + 6th observation) ÷ 2 = (4350 + 4390) ÷ 2 = Rs. 4370.
The wages occurring most often are Rs. 4250, Rs. 4350 and Rs. 4500; each occurs twice.
Therefore, the modes are Rs. 4250, Rs. 4350 and Rs. 4500.
solutions.answer: Arithmetic mean = Rs. 4370; median = Rs. 4370; modes = Rs. 4250, Rs. 4350 and Rs. 4500.

The arithmetic mean of the ages of 20 boys is 13 years, 4 months and 5 days. Find the sum of their ages. If one of the boys is of age exactly 15 years. What is the average age of the remaining boys?
steps: Taking 1 year = 12 months and 1 month = 30 days, 13 years 4 months 5 days = (13 × 360) + (4 × 30) + 5 = 4805 days.
Sum of ages of 20 boys = 20 × 4805 = 96100 days.
Age of the remaining 19 boys = 266 years 11 months 10 days − 15 years = 251 years 11 months 10 days.
Average age of the remaining boys = 90700/19 = 4773.68 days (approximately).
solutions.answer: The sum of their ages is 266 years 11 months 10 days. The average age of the remaining 19 boys is approximately 13 years 3 months 4 days.

solutions.question: Define histogram (unequal class limits).
steps: A histogram for unequal class limits is a graph of a frequency distribution made of adjacent rectangles.

mcqs.stem: Which data takes only some specific values?
rationales: Continuous data can take any value within a range, not only specific values.
Discrete data takes distinct, countable values.
Grouped data is data arranged into classes and may be continuous or discrete.
Ungrouped data is data presented without class groupings and does not specify the type of values it takes.

mcqs.stem: The number of times a value occurs in a data is called:
rationales: Frequency is the number of times a value occurs in a data set.
Relative frequency is the proportion or percentage of times a value occurs.
A class limit is an endpoint of a class interval.
Class boundaries separate adjacent class intervals.
The mean is the arithmetic average, not another name for the midpoint.
The median is the middle value of ordered data, not the midpoint of a class.
A class limit is an endpoint of a class interval.
The midpoint of a class interval is called its class mark.

mcqs.stem: Frequency polygon is also drawn /constructed by using:
rationales: A frequency polygon can be drawn by joining the midpoints at the tops of the histogram bars.
A bar graph is not the usual basis for constructing a frequency polygon.
Class boundaries define interval endpoints, but the polygon is plotted using class midpoints and frequencies.
Class limits define interval endpoints, but the polygon is plotted using class midpoints and frequencies.

mcqs.stem: The difference between the greatest value and the smallest value is called:
rationales: Class limits are the endpoints of class intervals.
A midpoint is the central value of an interval, not the difference between the data extremes.
Relative frequency is the proportion of observations in a category.
The range is the difference between the greatest and smallest values.

mcqs.stem: Measure of central tendency is used to find out the ________ of a data set.
rationales: Class boundaries separate adjacent class intervals and do not represent the centre of a data set.
Cumulative frequency is a running total of frequencies, not the centre of a data set.
A measure of central tendency identifies a middle or central value of the data set.
Frequency counts how often values occur, rather than identifying the centre.

mcqs.stem: If the mean of 5, 7, 8, 9 and x is 7.5, what will be the value of x?
rationales: If x were 10, the mean would be 7.8, not 7.5.
If x were 8, the mean would be 7.4, not 7.5.
The required total is 37.5, and 5 + 7 + 8 + 9 = 29, so x = 8.5.
If x were 5.8, the mean would be 6.96, not 7.5.

mcqs.stem: Find the mode of the given data: 2, 5, 8, 9, 0, 1, 3, 7 and 10
rationales: The value 5 occurs only once, so it is not the mode.
The value 7 occurs only once, so it is not the mode.
The value 0 occurs only once, so it is not the mode.
Every value occurs once, so the data set has no mode.

mcqs.stem: In a data the values (observations) which appears or occurs most often is called:
rationales: The mean is the arithmetic average of the observations.
The mode is the value that appears most often.
The median is the middle value after the observations are ordered.
The weighted mean is an average that gives different weights to observations.

mcqs.stem: Find the median of the given data: 110, 125, 122, 130, 124, 127 and 120
rationales: In order, the values are 110, 120, 122, 124, 125, 127, 130, so the middle value is 124.
120 is the second value in the ordered list, not the middle value.
125 is the fifth value in the ordered list, not the middle value.
127 is the sixth value in the ordered list, not the middle value.
